To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and implemented an adaptive and fully distributed duty cycle mechanism for CCN WNSs, which reduces the energy consumption of the forwarding process by up to 50% compared to a CCWNS approach with mostly on sensors.
the proposed mechanism is able to achieve a significant gain in terms of energy efficiency compared with a CCN approach that has all nodes in on state.

we propose an energy efficient forwarding mechanism for content centric wireless sensor networks that is fully distributed, and we prove that our solution is able to reduce the energy consumption of CCN WSN nodes by 50%, while keeping the same delay of the interest delivery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an adaptive duty cycle mechanism, based on the information centric networking paradigm, for energy efficient WSNs.
the design and evaluation of an adaptive duty cycle mechanism that can be applied to any ICN based WSN architecture to save energy and to improve the performance.
the design and evaluation of energy efficient mechanisms to support content centric networking on wireless sensor networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ADDC mechanism is a promising solution to reduce energy consumption in CCN based WSNs, while keeping a high user satisfaction.
our approach is an effective solution to reduce the energy consumption of forwarding while maintaining a high interest satisfaction and low delay.
the proposed mechanism is able to achieve a significant gain of the energy efficiency of the network while ensuring a high rate of interest satisfaction and keeping nearly the similar delay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADDC CCWSNs is a novel and effective approach that can be applied to ICN architectures to save energy in wireless sensor networks while achieving a high interest satisfaction.

, by exploiting the information centric networking architecture in a wireless sensor network, we achieve an adaptive and distributed duty cycle mechanism that saves energy and increases the interest satisfaction rate, while keeping a low delay.
we propose an energy efficient CCN WSN approach that can be used to save energy in WSNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of WSNs and ICN, the forwarding mechanism should be designed in order to adapt the duty cycle of each node to the traffic load of that node.
, in a content centric WSN, the energy efficiency of the system can be improved by tuning the duty cycles of nodes based on the number of unsatisfied interests they are storing in their PITs.
, in CCN WSN architectures, the PIT is a key component for energy efficient content delivery.
